messages:
maria (CS): Quick triage help — Lexa Labs onboarding hit a ramp and we're seeing intermittent 429s and occasional 401s during SDK init. They scaled from 2 -> 50 workers in staging, SDK v0.8.3 (node). Occurs within first 30s of warmup. Can we confirm if this is client-side fanout + preflight or our gateway?

jordan (SE): What do the error bodies/headers look like? 429 with a rate message or upstream 429 from a proxy? Any x-rate-limit headers showing?

maria (CS): Paste of their minimal log (redacted):

```
[2026-03-20T14:02:12.123Z] init: preflight start worker-17
[2026-03-20T14:02:12.456Z] http 401 POST /v1/sdk/init -> {error: "invalid_token", msg: "jwt expired"}
[2026-03-20T14:02:12.789Z] retry -> fetching ephemeral token
[2026-03-20T14:02:13.001Z] http 429 POST /v1/preflight -> {error: "rate_limited"} headers: x-rate-limit-reset=24
[2026-03-20T14:02:13.345Z] http 200 POST /v1/preflight
```

maria (CS): They also reported lots of short-lived connections (serverless containers) and http2 enabled in their agent.

sam (SDK): v0.8.3 had known preflight fanout behavior where parallel worker startups could trigger many simultaneous preflights and token refreshes. Two quick things: upgrade to v0.8.5 (hotfix) which adds randomized startup splay and token refresh coalescing, and as a workaround set the env var REDWOOD_SDK_PREFLIGHT_STAGGER_MS to something like "200-600" so workers stagger.

tina_ops: Also ask Lexa to check NTP on hosts — those 401s look like JWT skew in the times I've seen. If their clocks are >30s off, tokens can fail then retry and cause a fanout. Also enable keepAlive on the node http agent to reduce connection churn; our gateway's per-connection rate accounting can amplify fanout when every worker opens fresh connections.

jordan (SE): Are these requests coming from many ephemeral IPs (e.g., container scale-out across hosts)? If so, per-IP rate heuristics might bite. If behind a NAT/proxy, tell them to reuse a connection pool or run a small shared sidecar to prewarm.

maria (CS): Their setup: Kubernetes HPA with bursty start, 50 pods across 10 nodes, Node.js 18, HTTP/2 enabled via `--experimental-http2` polyfill, using our SDK init on process start. Config snippet they sent:

```
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, keepAlive: true, http2: true });
client.init({prefetch: true});
```

sam (SDK): OK — two additional mitigations without immediate SDK upgrade: (1) set `REDWOOD_PREFLIGHT_CONCURRENCY=2` to limit concurrent preflights per process, (2) keep `keepAlive: true` (good), and (3) if using http2, reduce streams per connection or fall back to http1 for preflight path. We'll push a quick patch to gate preflight concurrency per-process.

deploy-bot: Incident created CS-6421 (Lexa onboarding - SDK preflight storm). Assigned: eng-infra.

ravi (eng-infra): I'm on it — I'll temporarily raise the token-issue bucket for Lexa tenant for 2 hours to avoid churn during their ramp and add per-tenant tracing to see where the bursts land. Also will add a quick rule to prefer persistent connections for preflight routing.

maria (CS): Sent Lexa instructions: upgrade to v0.8.5, set `REDWOOD_SDK_PREFLIGHT_STAGGER_MS=350`, `REDWOOD_PREFLIGHT_CONCURRENCY=2`, ensure keepAlive true, and verify NTP. Asked them to retry a controlled ramp (5 -> 15 -> 30 -> 50 over 10m).

maria (CS): Update (14:18 UTC): after they upgraded and applied the env vars + enabled keepAlive, error rate dropped from ~7% to ~0.1% during the next ramp. 401s stopped after they fixed NTP on their hosts. I'll leave CS-6421 open for monitoring until Friday. :thumbsup:

maria (CS): Notes for runbook: onboarding checklist should include "staggered SDK preflight on scale-up" and a quick validation step for host time and persistent connection settings. I'll add to onboarding doc and ping devex to bake into the quickstart.
